summary: Rate gating recommendations for simultaneous webhook traffic and nightly cron flushes causing tenant 429s
description: Customer reports recurring 429 spikes during a daily window when their webhook ingestion traffic overlaps with a scheduled cron that performs bulk embedding flushes. This is a dedicated-customer account (DataNest) on a reserved pool. They observe the tenant-level quota is exhausted quickly and requests are rejected without clear prioritization between interactive webhooks and background flushes.
impact: Intermittent ingestion failures: failed webhooks returned 429s for ~3–7 minutes during the daily flush window. Business impact: several downstream pipelines retry aggressively, increasing downstream cost and causing data delivery delays for production customers.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure a tenant with a dedicated pool and two flows: high-rate webhook endpoint (/v1/webhook) and a nightly batch flush job (cron) that sends bulk embedding batches starting at 02:30 UTC.
2) Send ~350 concurrent webhook requests per second for sustained 5 minutes while the cron starts 30s into that window.
3) Observe 429s returned from the API gateway and token bucket exhaustion metrics in the quota dashboard.
logs:
[2025-02-10T02:30:12Z] ingress-proxy: conn=4823 route=/v1/webhook status=429 tenant=dn-182 token_balance=0
[2025-02-10T02:30:38Z] quota-service: tenant=dn-182 burst_pool=shared-burst credit_refill=0/60s
[2025-02-10T02:31:05Z] ingest-orch: cron-job=nightly-flush batches=18 concurrency=6 
[2025-02-10T02:33:47Z] ingress-proxy: conn=4859 route=/v1/webhook status=200 tenant=dn-182
investigation:
Support reproduced the pattern in a staging replica and confirmed tenant token bucket drained within 20–40s when background flush and webhook fanout overlapped. Observations:
- The dedicated pool uses a single burst pool for both interactive and background lanes.
- Background cron spawns multiple parallel multipart uploads which count against the same tenant burst credits.
- Healthcheck traffic from an internal k8s ingress controller also contributed ~10% of windowed usage.
- No route-level isolation configured for /v1/webhook vs background endpoints.
Hypothesis: shared burst pool and identical priority class for cron and webhook traffic cause background flush to evenly steal refill credits during the refill epoch, producing opaque 429 windows.
comments: 2025-02-10 — Aisha Patel (Support): Initial triage complete, reproduced in staging and collected token-bucket traces. Asking SRE for refill/epoch logs and whether pool splitting is available for dedicated customers.

2025-02-10 — SRE (Maya Fernandez): Confirmed refill epoch behavior. We saw a single refill epoch misalignment where cron jobs and interactive requests align and exhaust credits. Suggested options: route-level burst pools or lower priority for cron.
2025-02-11 — Customer (DataNest Ops - Evan Chu): We can shift cron time but want config guidance to avoid future collisions. Can we isolate webhook traffic?

2025-02-12 — Support (Liam O'Connell): Provided recommended config and a short-term mitigation (stagger cron + enable jitter). Customer agreed to staged rollout and asked for follow-up on console metrics to watch.
recommended_actions:
1) Split burst pools: create isolated burst pool (interactive-burst) for /v1/webhook route and a separate low-priority burst pool for background-flush routes.
2) Priority class: set cron jobs to priority=low so refill borrowing honors interactive lanes.
3) Refill alignment: increase refill granularity to 5s for dedicated pool or stagger cron start times by random jitter (30–90s).
4) Client-side: implement exponential backoff + jitter on webhook retries and cap concurrency on background flush to 2–3 parallel uploads.
5) Console: add quota heatmap dashboard for tenant burst pools and enable alerting on token_balance < 20% during refill epoch.
resolution: Workaround applied: customer staggered cron start by 90s and enabled 15% jitter on the cron runners; set background flush concurrency to 2. Support created a route-level isolation change request for the dedicated pool (internal ticket INT-88901) and a PR to the rate-limiter to support per-route burst pools for dedicated customers. After changes, token-bucket drain events disappeared during the window and webhook success rates returned to baseline. Customer to schedule a follow-up in 7 days to observe weekly cron windows.
related_notes: Linked runbook: rate-pools-splitting (Confluence). Slack thread: #support (thread TS-4l9j2) contains traces and Grafana links. Internal follow-up INT-88901 tracks per-route burst pool rollout and console UX improvements.
next_steps:
1) Engineering to ship PR-427 to enable per-route burst pools for dedicated tenants.
2) Support to monitor DataNest metrics for 7 days and close when stable.
3) Product to review default priority for scheduled background jobs and add a console toggle to isolate background lanes.
customer_followup: Support scheduled a 30-minute call for 2025-02-14 to review the dashboard and confirm stable behavior. Customer requested a postmortem-style note summarizing actions taken and configuration snippets for their ops runbook.
